research_rationale:
EO 11039 (signed Aug. 3, 1962; 27 FR 7755), read in full in the held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11039.txt, 1,294 chars), amends EO 10974 (Nov. 8, 1961, 26 FR 10585, which I also read in full in jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10974.txt) 'effective as of July 1, 1962': item (1) adds the FY1963 appropriation to the section 5 funding source; item (2) replaces the last sentence of EO 10974 (its section 7 sentence 'The Commission shall terminate not later than 120 days after the date of its transmittal of its principal report') with 'The Commission shall terminate as of November 1, 1962.' That sentence is a fixed sunset date of the Commission, not a report deadline; the unamended April 30, 1962 report date in EO 10974 sec. 7 is not used as an end. The order's three pieces (the amending lead, item 1 funding, item 2 termination) all operate only through EO 10974's Commission and end when it ends on 1962-11-01 by the order's own words (TERM record own_terms_sunset_date). Searches: the OFR catalog (1937 on) lists only 'Amended by: EO 11039' on EO 10974 and only 'Amends: EO 10974' on EO 11039, no later amendment, revocation or extension; the three machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, OFR catalog) have 0 hits for this order; my own scan of the held FR order texts for '10974' finds only EO 10974, EO 11039 and an unrelated contents-page number in EO 9602. Limit: no held source gives the date the Commission transmitted its principal report; that does not matter because EO 11039 itself, made effective as of July 1, 1962 and signed Aug. 3, 1962, replaced the 120-day termination sentence and treats the Commission as then existing.

The 'as of November 1, 1962' phrase fixes the date on which the Commission ceases; I take 1962-11-01 as the effective date.","independent_command_check":"None survives the Commission: the lead and item (1) only change sections of EO 10974 (the Commission's authority to be paid from FY1963 funds); item (2) is itself the termination. research_rationale:
EO 11756 (signed Dec. 30, 1973; 39 FR 781, Jan. 3, 1974), read in full in the held FR text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11756.txt), is a single-clause order under 5 U.S.C. 8335(c) exempting Whitney Gillilland, Vice Chairman of the Civil Aeronautics Board, from mandatory retirement for age 'until December 31, 1974'. It is a fixed-term grant that ends by its own terms on 1974-12-31 (TERM record own_terms_until_event, chars 1017-1267). The only later order naming him is EO 11824 (signed Dec. 28, 1974; 40 FR 751), which I read in full from the held actor text: it recites that Mr. Gillilland 'was exempted through December 31, 1974, by Executive Order No. 11756 and has continued to serve on the Civil Aeronautics Board during 1974', finds the public interest requires that he 'continue to be exempted', and issues a fresh exemption 'until June 30, 1975' under the same subsection. It does not amend, extend or revoke EO 11756, and it positively confirms that the exemption ran its full term (no early departure). Searches: OFR catalog lists no disposition note on either order; U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches have 0 hits; my own scan of held FR order texts and APP texts for 'Gillilland' finds only EO 11756 and EO 11824. Authority check: 5 U.S.C. 8335(c) is the statutory basis cited in both orders; no held source shows its repeal before the stated end.

The until-date is the fixed term of the grant, not a deadline or not-later-than bound on some other act.","independent_command_check":"The order has one operative command, the time-limited exemption. By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of

“(b) The Mission shall, in accordan ce with the Foreign A ssistance A ct of 1961,  
as amended, including Part II, Chapter 6 thereof, the Joint Resolution of  
O ctober 13 ,1 9 7 5  (Public Law  94-110, 89 Stat. 572, 22 U.S.C. 2441 note), and the  
provisions of this Order, assist in the implementation of the provisions of

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Superseded by amendment: EO 12227 amends sections 1(b) and 1(c) of EO 11896 'to read as follows' with an entirely new paragraph (b), replacing the paragraph EO 12150 inserted. Actor EO 12227; no stated effective date, so effective on signing 1980-07-22.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By the authority vested in me as President of the United States of America, 
including Chapter 6 of Part II of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, as 
amended (22 U.S.C. 2348, 2348a.-2348c.J, Section 1(b) of Executive Order No. 
11896 of January 13,1976, is hereby amended to read:
“(b) The Mission shall, in accordance with the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, 
as amended, including Part II, Chapter 6 thereof, the Joint Resolution of 
October 13,1975 (Public Law 94-110, 89 Stat. 572, 22 U.S.C. 2441 note), and the 
provisions of this Order, carry out the duties and responsibilities of the United 
States Government to implement the “United States Proposal for the Early 
Warning System in Sinai” in connection with the Basic Agreement between 
Egypt and Israel, signed on September 4, 1975, and the Annex to the Basic 
Agreement, as superseded by the Treaty of Peace between the Arab Republic 
of Egypt and the State of Israel, signed on March 26, 1979, and Article VII of 
the Appendix to Annex I of the Treaty of Peace, subject to broad policy 
guidance received through the Assistant to the President for National Security 
Affairs, and the continuous supervision and general direction of the Secretary 
of State pursuant to Section 622(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, as 
amended (22 U.S.C. 2382(c)).”.

EO 12150 (signed July 23, 1979; 44 FR 43455), read in full in the held FR text, has one operative sentence: Section 1(b) of EO 11896 (Jan. 13, 1976, establishing the U.S. Sinai Support Mission; I read its sec. 1 in the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11896.txt) 'is hereby amended to read' a new paragraph (b) that redefines the Mission's duties by reference to the 1975 Basic Agreement 'as superseded by the Treaty of Peace' of March 26, 1979 and Article VII of the Appendix to Annex I. EO 12227 (signed July 22, 1980; 45 FR 49237), read in full from the held actor text, states that 'Sections 1(b) and 1(c) of Executive Order No. 11896 ..., as amended, are hereby further amended to read as follows' and prints an entirely new paragraph (b) (the Mission 'assist[s] in the implementation of the provisions of Annex I and the Appendix to Annex I' of the Treaty by verification tasks). The text inserted by EO 12150 therefore ceased to exist in EO 11896 when EO 12227 took effect; the OFR catalog confirms both as amendments of EO 11896. EO 12227 states no effective date and has no savings or transition clause, so it took effect on signing, 1980-07-22. Later events (EO 12357 of Apr. 6, 1982 adding wind-down sec. 2(g); EO 12553 of Feb. 25, 1986 revoking EO 11896 and its amendments) post-date the first end and are not used. Searches: OFR catalog 'Amended by' list for EO 11896 (EO 12150, 12227, 12357) shows no amendment of (b) between 1979-07-23 and 1980-07-22; U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches have 0 hits.

Federal Register / Vol. 44, No. 144 / Wednesday, July 25,1979 / Presidential Documents 43455
Presidential Documents
Executive Order 12150 of July 23, 1979
United States Sinai Support Mission
By the authority vested in me as President of the United States of America, 
including Chapter 6 of Part II of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, as 
amended (22 U.S.C. 2348, 2348a.-2348c.J, Section 1(b) of Executive Order No. 
11896 of January 13,1976, is hereby amended to read:
“(b) The Mission shall, in accordance with the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, 
as amended, including Part II, Chapter 6 thereof, the Joint Resolution of 
October 13,1975 (Public Law 94-110, 89 Stat. 572, 22 U.S.C. 2441 note), and the 
provisions of this Order, carry out the duties and responsibilities of the United 
States Government to implement the “United States Proposal for the Early 
Warning System in Sinai” in connection with the Basic Agreement between 
Egypt and Israel, signed on September 4, 1975, and the Annex to the Basic 
Agreement, as superseded by the Treaty of Peace between the Arab Republic 
of Egypt and the State of Israel, signed on March 26, 1979, and Article VII of 
the Appendix to Annex I of the Treaty of Peace, subject to broad policy 
guidance received through the Assistant to the President for National Security 
Affairs, and the continuous supervision and general direction of the Secretary 
of State pursuant to Section 622(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, as 
amended (22 U.S.C. 2382(c)).”.
THE WHITE HOUSE,
